name: Commentaries from the Perseus Digital Library (open-source TEI distribution)
licence_name: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 United States (CC BY-SA 3.0 US)
version: Each commentary file records its own source URL and commit
what_we_use: Commentary notes shown in the Reader's Scholarship tab: Servius on Vergil; Conington and Nettleship on the Aeneid; the anonymous commentary on Ovid's Heroides; Simmons on Metamorphoses XIII-XIV; Donkin on Cicero Pro Roscio Amerino; Merrill on Catullus; Shorey on Horace; Gildersleeve on Pindar; Monro on the Odyssey XIII-XXIV; Merry and Riddell on the Odyssey I-XII; Seymour on the Iliad I-VI; Leaf on the Iliad; Allen and Sikes on the Homeric Hymns; Jebb on Sophocles Ajax; Cope on Aristotle's Rhetoric; How and Wells on Herodotus; Goodwin on Demosthenes On the Crown; Paley and Sandys on Demosthenes private orations; Sharpley on the Olynthiacs.
notes: Taken through the CLTK mirrors https://github.com/cltk/lat_text_perseus and https://github.com/cltk/grc_text_perseus. Because the licence is share-alike, these notes stay under CC BY-SA 3.0 US.

name: JSTOR Early Journal Content, via the Internet Archive
licence_name: Pre-1923 journal articles released by JSTOR as Early Journal Content
version: Offline index built 2026-09-19 from the Early Journal Content full texts fetched from the Internet Archive on 2026-09-14 (data/citation_index/citations.db); the companion index of citations of inscriptions and papyri built 2026-10-09 (document_citations.db)
what_we_use: The site's own index of passage citations found in the running text of 24 journals, 1827 to 1922: The Biblical World, Modern Language Notes, The Classical Weekly, The American Journal of Philology, The Classical Journal, Classical Philology, Rheinisches Museum für Philologie (1827 to 1866), The Jewish Quarterly Review, The Journal of English and Germanic Philology, PMLA, The American Journal of Semitic Languages and Literatures, Hebraica, American Journal of Archaeology (and its predecessor), Modern Philology, The Harvard Theological Review, Journal of Biblical Literature, Transactions of the American Philological Association, Harvard Studies in Classical Philology, The Journal of Germanic Philology, Studies in Philology (to 1922) and Hermes (1866 to 1869). 29,055 articles were read; 5,193 of them cite one of 437 works held here, 33,386 citations in all. The same texts yield 956 sentences from 288 articles that cite 742 of the inscriptions and papyri, shown on the document's page. The Reader's Scholarship tab and the document page show the citing article, the sentence that cites, and a link to the article on JSTOR.
notes: Only the citing sentence is shown, never the article text. The Early Journal Content is the set of journal issues published in the United States before 1923, or elsewhere before 1870, that JSTOR released for free reuse; the Internet Archive holds the copies we read. Index built offline, no request-time calls.

name: Wikidata
licence_name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 (public domain dedication)
version: Query of 2026-10-09 (battles, sieges, treaties and other dated events of the ancient Mediterranean, with their labels, dates, places and participants)
what_we_use: The list of events on the Events page, each event's name, date, place and participants, and the link to its Wikipedia article. The opening paragraph of the English Wikipedia article (CC BY-SA 4.0) is read by the offline language model when it judges whether a passage tells of the event. It is not shown on the site.
notes: Places are matched to Pleiades through the Wikidata place items. Passages are chosen by the names in the Wikidata record and sorted by an offline language model that no person has checked; the page says so.

name: Photographs of inscriptions and papyri (linked, not copied)
licence_name: Each photograph stays on the institution's own site under that institution's terms; Tesserae stores only the address

Links to hosts that no longer answer are not shown.
notes: No image file is copied to our server.

name: Cleveland Museum of Art, Open Access (Greek and Roman Art department)
licence_name: Creative Commons Zero 1.0 (CC0)
version: Open Access API, department "Greek and Roman Art", all 688 records
what_we_use: The catalogue record of each object that has a curator's description: title, culture, date, technique, find spot, inscriptions, the description, the credit line, the address of the museum's own page and, where the record's share_license_status is CC0, the address of the museum's web image. 177 coin records are left out because coins have their own collection.
notes: The API page says: "To the extent possible under law, The Cleveland Museum of Art has waived all copyright and related or neighboring rights to this dataset using Creative Commons Zero." and "While all data in the dataset is released with a CC0 designation, only artworks with the CC0 share_license_status will additionally provide access to CC0 images." Every one of the 688 records reads CC0. Images are linked from the museum's server and not stored here.

name: Art Institute of Chicago, public API data dump (Arts of Greece, Rome, and Byzantium)
licence_name: Creative Commons Zero 1.0 (CC0) for the records, Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0) for the description field
version: artic-api-data.tar.bz2 from artic-api-data.s3.amazonaws.com, department "Arts of Greece, Rome, and Byzantium" (2,197 records)
what_we_use: The catalogue record of each Greek, Roman or Etruscan object with a description: title, place of origin, date, medium, classification, the description, the short description, inscriptions, the credit line, the address of the museum's own page and, only where the record's public domain flag is true, the address of the museum's web image. Coins, Byzantine and later objects are left out.
notes: The API documentation says: "The description field in this response is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 Generic License (CC-By) and the Terms and Conditions of artic.edu. All other data in this response is licensed under a Creative Commons Zero (CC0) 1.0 designation and the Terms and Conditions of artic.edu." Each card names the museum as the source of the description. Images are linked from the museum's server and not stored here.

name: Smithsonian Open Access (National Museum of Natural History, Department of Anthropology)
licence_name: Creative Commons Zero 1.0 (CC0)
version: Smithsonian Open Access metadata repository on AWS (smithsonian-open-access.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com, unit nmnhanthro), 529,663 records read
what_we_use: The catalogue notes of the Greek, Roman and Etruscan objects (vases, lamps, figurines, casts) that carry a note of at least 40 characters: title, culture, place, object type, the note and the address of the museum's own record. Notes that only cite a publication or that say they were copied from another institution's database are left out.
notes: Every one of the 1,268 Greek, Roman or Etruscan records reads "metadata_usage": {"access": "CC0"}. The public API key allowed ten requests an hour and was exhausted, so the same records were read from the open-access bucket. The records in the bucket carry no image address, so no image is shown.
